macro_summary: Markets are navigating a hawkish macro backdrop after August payrolls came in sharply hotter than expected (+162K vs. +53K consensus), pushing the 10-year yield to 4.78% (multi-year highs) and lifting Fed hike odds for the September 16 FOMC decision to ~58%. The S&P 500 sits at ~7,708, roughly flat over the past month but up ~19% YoY, while tech-heavy indices face multiple compression from rising rates. Meanwhile, WTI crude holds near $91/bbl on Iran conflict-related Hormuz supply disruption, and an Apple product event on September 9 provides a hard-dated, non-macro catalyst to watch alongside the Fed.

ideas.name: Apple Inc.
ideas.thesis: Appeared in all 6 of 6 overnight screens with unanimous high conviction. Apple's September 9 event is a hard-dated, 4-day catalyst featuring CEO John Ternus's debut and a potential first-ever foldable 'iPhone Ultra' (est. $2,099–$2,299 ASP per TrendForce) — the most significant iPhone form-factor change since the iPhone X. Morgan Stanley projects the foldable alone could generate ~$14B in December-quarter revenue, while consensus price targets of ~$328 imply 4.5% upside from current ~$314–$320 levels (stock dipped ~2.6% Friday, offering a pre-event entry). A defined-risk call spread expiring September 19 is the preferred structure to bracket the event window without absorbing binary overnight exposure or full premium risk at 35.5x forward P/E.
ideas.catalyst: Apple iPhone 18 launch event — September 9, 2026 at 10am PT / 1pm ET; pre-orders expected September 12; retail availability September 18
ideas.edge: Street-high target of $400 (Rothschild Redburn) implies 27%+ upside; Morgan Stanley projects foldable iPhone generates ~$14B in December-quarter revenue alone; stock is ~7% below its 52-week high of $344.57 after Friday's -2.6% dip, creating a pre-event entry discount
ideas.bull_case: Foldable iPhone Ultra launches at $2,099+ ASP, structurally lifting revenue mix and triggering a re-rating; new CEO Ternus narrative + surprise product execution drives a sell-side upgrade wave and pre-order momentum through September 18 availability.
ideas.bear_case: Foldable reveal is delayed or underwhelms (spec leaks already priced in), triggering a classic sell-the-news reaction; 35.5x forward P/E leaves little margin for disappointment and FOMC rate hike risk on September 16 could pressure the multiple within days of the event.

ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ideas.thesis: Appeared in all 6 of 6 overnight screens (5 high conviction, 1 medium). NVDA reported a blowout Q2 FY2027 on August 26 — EPS of $2.46 (+128% YoY, beat consensus) — yet trades at a forward P/E of only ~23.9x, a 14% premium to the S&P 500 despite sell-side consensus projecting a 58% revenue CAGR through FY2029 and a disclosed $1 trillion order book for 2026–2027. Friday's broad market selloff on hot jobs data pushed the stock back ~4.8% from post-earnings highs, creating a swing re-entry ahead of the September 10 ex-dividend date and Vera Rubin GPU ramp in H2 2026. The primary risk is the September 16 FOMC decision — a surprise hike could broadly compress growth multiples.
ideas.catalyst: Ex-dividend date September 10, 2026 ($0.25/share); Vera Rubin GPU shipment ramp H2 2026; FOMC decision September 16 as key risk event
ideas.edge: Forward P/E of 23.9x is only a 14% premium to the S&P 500 — historically the cheapest NVDA has traded relative to the market since the AI rally began — despite 58% projected annual revenue CAGR through FY2029 and a $1 trillion order book vs. ~$253B trailing revenue
ideas.bull_case: Post-earnings momentum resumes as the market digests the magnitude of the revenue backlog and Vera Rubin GPU ramp; FOMC holds on September 16, relieving rate pressure on growth multiples and allowing NVDA to recover toward analyst targets.
ideas.bear_case: A September 16 FOMC hike combined with 10-year yields near 4.78% compresses growth stock multiples broadly; any sign of data center capex deceleration from hyperscaler customers could derail the backlog narrative despite strong reported numbers.

ideas.name: SK Hynix Inc. (ADR)
ideas.thesis: Appeared in all 6 of 6 overnight screens, though with mixed conviction (2 high, 4 medium), reflecting its high-volatility ADR nature. SKHY is NVIDIA's primary HBM3e supplier and the highest-beta pure-play on AI memory demand — directly leveraged to NVDA's disclosed $267B memory spend roadmap through 2029. The stock ripped from ~$135–$140 lows in early August to $177 on September 4 (+8.14% that session alone), supported by a Bernstein Buy reaffirmation, a 40 trillion KRW share buyback, Temasek capital injection, and Q2 operating margins of 76% (+479bps QoQ). The swing target is the $178 August peak, with structural support from the buyback program.
ideas.catalyst: Bernstein Buy reaffirmed September 4, 2026; NVDA's $267B memory spend roadmap through 2029 confirmed; ongoing 40 trillion KRW buyback program and Dalian NAND plant restart
ideas.edge: Q2 operating margin of 76% (+479bps QoQ); global memory chip sales +123.6% YoY; stock recovered from $135–$140 lows to $177 — swing target at $178 August peak with buyback providing a structural floor. Bernstein Buy reiteration adds institutional signal.
ideas.bull_case: Nvidia HBM demand accelerates into H2 2026 GPU ramp, memory sector momentum sustains, and SKHY breaks above $178 August highs toward prior resistance; buyback and Temasek capital provide downside support on any pullbacks.
ideas.bear_case: ADR has exhibited 10%+ single-day swings (dropped sharply post its own late-July earnings call); FOMC rate hike on September 16 could trigger broad risk-off selling; options liquidity on the ADR is limited, making defined-risk structures difficult to execute — verify before sizing.

ideas.name: Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund
ideas.thesis: Appeared in 3 of 6 overnight screens as a macro hedge and swing trade. WTI crude holds near $91/bbl driven by Iran conflict Strait of Hormuz supply disruption (+31.4% from July 6 to September 1), making energy the only S&P sector up ~21% in Q3 2026 and the leading sector YTD. XLE's integrated major constituents (ExxonMobil, Chevron) trade at 8–12% free cash flow yields with 3%+ dividends, providing a valuation floor. The September 16 FOMC decision is a dual catalyst — a hike reinforces energy as an inflation hedge while a hold removes the primary sector headwind of yield-driven multiple compression.
ideas.catalyst: FOMC rate decision September 16, 2026 (hike = inflation hedge thesis strengthens; hold = sector re-rates higher); Iran conflict Strait of Hormuz supply disruption ongoing with WTI at ~$91/bbl
ideas.edge: XLE constituents trade at 8–12% FCF yields vs. broad market average; energy is the only S&P sector positive in Q3 2026; WTI crude has a structural supply deficit with Hormuz risk premium intact; XLE yields ~2.5–3%+ in income buffer. A covered call overlay can monetize elevated sector volatility.
ideas.bull_case: Iran supply disruption persists into Q4 keeping oil above $90; FOMC holds on September 16, driving a relief rally across risk assets while energy retains its inflation-hedge premium and FCF yield support attracts institutional rotation.
ideas.bear_case: A diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict removes the geopolitical supply premium sharply; a Fed hike triggers broad risk-off selling that overwhelms energy's defensive characteristics; dollar strengthens on hawkish dot plot, pressuring crude denominated in USD.

ideas.name: Invesco QQQ Trust (Nasdaq-100 ETF)
ideas.thesis: Appeared in 2 of 6 overnight screens as a defined-risk macro hedge around the September 16 FOMC binary. With ~58% market-implied probability of a 25bp hike following the +162K vs. +53K NFP beat, and the 10-year yield already at 4.78% (multi-year high), the tech-heavy QQQ is the most rate-sensitive major ETF and faces the sharpest compression risk if a hike is confirmed with a hawkish dot plot. A put spread or straddle/strangle expiring after September 16 captures either tail of the binary cleanly. Works as an options strategy only — not a directional stock position.
ideas.catalyst: FOMC rate decision September 16, 2026 at 2pm ET — dot plot and SEP released same day; ~58% market-implied probability of 25bp hike post-NFP beat of +162K vs. +53K expected
ideas.edge: 10-year yield at 4.78% already pressuring growth multiples; a hike + hawkish dot plot would be first rate increase in this cycle — QQQ put spread captures meaningful drawdown risk. A surprise hold would spark a sharp Nasdaq relief rally. Coin-flip odds create a binary where options may be mispriced for the magnitude of either move.
ideas.bull_case: Fed holds on September 16 and dot plot signals an extended pause — tech multiples re-expand sharply, QQQ surges from compressed levels, and straddle profits on the upside leg.
ideas.bear_case: If the market has already priced the hike fully, QQQ may not sell off as sharply as expected on confirmation — options premium decay erodes the put spread value if QQQ stays range-bound into and through the decision.
